text:
sarah (AE): Quick sync — ACME wants a 6-week trial to validate relevance + latency for their support summarization use case. Need to lock scope, success criteria, and who covers which weeks. Can SEs confirm bandwidth?

mike (SE): I can cover week 0-2 for setup + prompt tuning. 6-10 hours/wk. Will need dedicated GPU for perf runs on weeks 3-4 if we do throughput tests.

alex (Eng): For perf we should run both hosted and dedicated configs. I can own the perf run scripts and KV-cache checks. Need the model artifacts and expected avg sequence length.

sarah (AE): Expected seq len ~800 tokens for full threads, typical avg 250. Primary success metric: F1 on entity extraction >= 0.78 and 95th pct latency < 450ms for P50 < 120ms. Also cost target: <$0.015/token at peak.

vijay (PS): Noted. For pricing: customer is asking if we can do a short dedicated capacity trial discount. I can surface a 4-week reduced rate for the Dedicated SKU if we commit to 4 weeks. CC @sarah (AE).

olga (Security): Heads up — they requested latest SOC2/ISO cert snapshot and answers to the encryption section in their questionnaire (Q12-Q18). I can send a redacted cert and a short writeup. Need the list of endpoints used in the trial (hosted vs private).

mike (SE): On prompts/evals: can we get a seed eval set (50 threads) from ACME by EOD Friday? I’ll run baseline prompts and iterate. Also want to run an eval harness:

mike (SE): ```
# quick perf run example
python perf/run.py --model redwood-1.0 --seq 800 --concurrency 8 --duration 300
# eval harness
python eval/run_eval.py --input acme_seed.json --strategy reranking --output results.json
```

alex (Eng): That looks good. I’ll add an automated KV-cache warmup step to the perf script. Will post the PR to infra repo by Tue.

sarah (AE): Timeline proposal: week 0 (kickoff + certs + dataset ingest), week 1-2 (prompt tuning + baseline quality), week 3 (scale perf tests), week 4 (A/B with quantized variant + cost calc), week 5 (finalize report + handover). If anyone needs more time, flag now.

vijay (PS): I put together a short success criteria checklist for sales signoff:
- Quality: macro F1 >= 0.78 on eval set
- Latency: 95p < 450ms in target config
- Cost: projected unit cost < $0.015/token
- Reliability: no more than 1% error rate on streaming responses

mike (SE): Ownership: I’ll do prompt tuning and baseline quality. Alex does perf scripts and infra. Vijay will negotiate dedicated pricing. Olga does security artifacts. Sarah owns customer comms and final acceptance.

sarah (AE): Blockers: 1) ACME legal wants a data handling clause tweak (we have a template but may need legal). 2) They asked about on-prem option for PHI — we should confirm Private deployment lead times.

olga (Security): For PHI: if they need on-prem, we need a scoping call — private deploy typically 6–8 weeks depending on network. I can join but will need the questionnaire answers in advance.

alex (Eng): Can someone confirm whether we should run quantized q4 8-bit variant for cost calc? That changes perf expectations.

vijay (PS): Yes, include both FP16 hosted baseline and 8-bit quantized dedicated variant in the cost/latency matrix. I’ll include that in the pricing note.

sarah (AE): Can we get a quick resource commit today so I can tell ACME? Need SE coverage (10 hrs/wk weeks 0-3, 6 hrs/wk weeks 4-5), Eng perf (20 hrs total across weeks 2-4), Security artifacts by Wed.

mike (SE): Confirmed for my hours.

alex (Eng): I can allocate the perf hours.

olga (Security): I’ll send the cert + partial questionnaire answers by Wed morning.

vijay (PS): I’ll draft the discounted commitment proposal and send to Sarah for review by EOD.

sarah (AE): Great. Action items summary:
- ACME to share 50-thread eval set by Fri (ACME)
- Mike: baseline prompts + evals (due end week 2)
- Alex: perf scripts + KV warmup PR (due Tue)
- Vijay: pricing note + dedicated trial proposal (EOD)
- Olga: security docs + Q12-Q18 answers (Wed)
- Sarah: kickoff invite + legal loop for data clause (today)

mike (SE): Small question — for the eval scoring, do we use strict token-level F1 or relaxed span matching? I prefer relaxed for entity overlaps.

vijay (PS): Use relaxed span matching for initial pass; strict for final report. Document both.

sarah (AE): Ok locking that. Can someone drop a calendar invite for the kickoff tomorrow 10am PT?

deploy-bot: new-meeting created by sarah (AE) — "ACME trial kickoff" Tue 10:00 PT (link: https://calendar.internal/meet/abc123)

alex (Eng): Added checklist in the shared doc: https://redwood.internal/sales/acme-trial-runway — please add your items.

mike (SE): Added eval script notes and a short prompt appendix.

olga (Security): Uploaded certs to the secure share (link redacted).

sarah (AE): Thanks team — I’ll update ACME after kickoff. If any blocker pops up, @channel, ping ASAP. :thumbsup:
